info.title: Lookup, Media, Search & Inventory
info.description:
# Partner Integrator API
Authenticated, usage-metered access to bookable travel inventory for API integrators. Query
properties, availability and rates programmatically at scale under
/api/partner/{managingEntityIdentifier}/. Requests are counted and rate-limited per account:
a free tier applies until you subscribe to the metered paid tier. See the Partner API
pricing & SLA page for current limits, per-request pricing and terms.

Every call carries **two** gRPC metadata headers:

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `authorization` | `Bearer <token>` — the same token the REST surface accepts |
| `wink-managing-entity-id` | The account you are calling on behalf of |

Authorization is per account: the account named in `wink-managing-entity-id` is checked for `INVENTORY:READ`, and metered usage is billed to it. Omit the header and the call fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; name an account you do not hold `INVENTORY:READ` on and it fails with `PERMISSION_DENIED`.

The account is a header rather than a request field so that it is known before the request body is read — which is what lets quota and rate-limit checks reject a call without decoding it. Request messages therefore have no account field, and setting one is not possible.

### Generating a client

You call this API with a generated gRPC client, not with `curl`. Wink publishes the
schema two ways:

- **Server reflection** — the server describes itself, so `grpcurl`, Postman and Insomnia discover the schema at runtime with nothing to download. Reflection needs the same bearer token as any other call.
- **The `.proto` files**, if you would rather vendor the schema and generate ahead of time.

```bash
# Reflection describes the schema and needs only the token — it is not account-scoped.
grpcurl -H "authorization: Bearer $WINK_TOKEN" partner.wink.travel:443 list

# Every actual call additionally needs the account header.
grpcurl -H "authorization: Bearer $WINK_TOKEN" \
        -H "wink-managing-entity-id: $WINK_ACCOUNT_ID" \
        -d '{"urlName": "bangkok-thailand", "type": "CITY"}' \
        partner.wink.travel:443 wink.partner.v1.Lookup/Get
```

[Generating a Wink gRPC client](https://wink.travel/developers/rest-and-grpc/) walks through it with our schema. For the language-specific toolchain, see the official [gRPC quick starts](https://grpc.io/docs/languages/).

> **This is a gRPC API, not a REST API.** Each operation is listed at the HTTP/2 path the transport really uses (`/package.Service/Method`, always `POST`), and the schemas are the [proto3 JSON mapping](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/) of each message — so the contract is readable and model generation is correct. But these endpoints are **not callable with an ordinary HTTP client**: a real request body is a length-prefixed protobuf frame. Use a generated gRPC client, or the `.proto` schema published via server reflection.

### Errors

Failures arrive as a gRPC status code in the response **trailers**, not as an HTTP status code:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | The request was malformed, or a required field was missing. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Bearer token missing, expired or invalid. |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | The token is valid but lacks the required grant on the account. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | No record matched (only on operations that resolve a single record). |
| `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | Quota exceeded. Carries `retry-after` and `x-ratelimit-*` trailers — back off by the value given. |

tags.name: Search
tags.description:
Search Wink's bookable property inventory and get live prices — the paid Partner Search API.

Six ways to find properties: by map position, by city, or ranked by agency, city, country or globally.
All six return the same page shape, so one result renderer serves every entry point.

These endpoints return PRICES, not property content. Each result carries just enough to render a list row
— name, location, star rating, one image — plus the prices themselves. Descriptions, galleries, addresses,
room detail, amenities and policies come from the Content service, which you should cache per property and
refresh when `last_update` changes. That split keeps search responses small and fast, and it means
property content has exactly one source of truth.

Every call needs an authenticated token with `INVENTORY:READ` on the account you pass, and is billed in
hotel-day units: (properties actually returned) x min(itinerary nights, 90). You are charged for what comes
back, not for what you asked for — a request for 50 results that matches 3 properties bills 3 properties.

Prices are live and are not cached. Treat a result as valid for the length of a user's session.

tags.name: Lookup
tags.description:
Find the destinations you can query and sell through Wink: properties, cities, countries, islands
and attractions.

The usual flow is two calls. Use **Search** as your user types to offer suggestions, then take
the `urlName` of whichever one they pick and pass it to **Get** to resolve the full record and
confirm you are allowed to sell it.

Both calls are free. They count towards your per-minute call quota but are not hotel-day
metered, so you can drive an autocomplete from Search without affecting your bill.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description:
Look up live prices for a property you already know — the paid Partner Inventory API.

Search finds properties and returns each one's best offer. Inventory is the next step: given a property,
return EVERY priced offer for the requested dates and occupancy, plus a rate calendar for planning across
a date range.

These endpoints return PRICES, not property content. Names, descriptions, galleries, addresses, amenities,
policies, restaurants, spas and everything else come from the Content service — call it once per property,
cache the answer, and refresh when `last_update` changes. That keeps these responses small and means
property content has exactly one source of truth.

Every call needs an authenticated token with `INVENTORY:READ` on the account you name in the
`wink-managing-entity-id` metadata header, and is billed in hotel-day units.

Prices are live and are not cached. Treat a result as valid for the length of a user's session.

tags.name: Media
tags.description:
Retrieve published property and inventory media through Wink — the paid Partner Media API.

Source of truth is the same published, entitlement-checked galleries the REST twin serves: your
sales-channel inventory for the property, never the internal media catalog. Key every asset you store
on `media_identifier`, not on any URL — see the field docs on `MediaAsset` and `MediaUrlSet` for
why URLs are not permanent.

Both calls require an authenticated token with `INVENTORY:READ` on the account you pass, and are
billed 1 unit per property whose media is actually returned.

post.description:
Search by map position

Find properties near a point or inside map bounds. Set one member of the `area` oneof: `location` with
`search_filters.radius_in_meters` for "near here", or `bounds` for "everything in this viewport".

Because `area` is a oneof, setting one member clears the other — you cannot send both. Returns
INVALID_ARGUMENT if you send neither.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Search by city

Find available properties in or around a city, identified by its GeoNames id — the same id the Lookup
service returns for a destination.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Rank a management agency's properties

Return the properties represented by one management agency, ordered by the scoring type you choose.
Unlike the other ranked calls this one takes no search filters.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Rank a city's properties

Return properties in or around a city by url name, ordered by the scoring type you choose.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Rank a country's properties

Return properties within a country, ordered by the scoring type you choose.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Rank properties worldwide

Return the best-scoring properties across the whole platform. Use this for editorial and discovery
surfaces rather than for a destination search.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Search by term

Typeahead search across destinations. Send the partial text your user has typed and render
the results as suggestions.

Terms shorter than 3 characters return an empty list rather than an error, so it is safe to
call on every keystroke. At most 50 results are returned, most relevant first.

Suggestions are not filtered by your sales channel — a property you cannot sell may still
appear here. Get is where that is enforced.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Look up by URL slug

Resolve one destination from its URL slug and type — for example `bangkok-thailand` plus
DESTINATION_TYPE_CITY. Use it after Search, or whenever you already hold a Wink destination slug in your own
routing.

Both fields are required, because a slug is only unique within a type.

Returns PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_NOT_FOUND when nothing matches. For a property that exists but sits outside your sales
channel it returns PERMISSION_DENIED instead, so you can tell "not yours to sell" apart from
"no such destination".

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Prices for one property

Returns every offer bookable at this property for the requested dates and occupancy, cheapest first.
Identify the property by `property_id` or by `url_name` — set exactly one.

Billed as min(itinerary nights, 90) hotel-day units, whether or not anything is available.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Prices for several properties

The same lookup for many properties at once, resolved in parallel. Each entry carries its own dates and
occupancy, so you can price different stays in one call.

Billed as the SUM over entries of min(that entry's nights, 90) — a batch costs exactly what the same
entries would cost individually, so batching is a latency optimisation rather than a discount.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Rate calendar

The best available rate for every check-in/check-out combination across a date range — what you need to
render a "cheapest night to stay" calendar without one call per date.

Billed as `period_in_days` hotel-day units.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
Get one property's media gallery

Return a single property's published media — the property itself plus every bookable inventory
item entitled to your sales channel (guest rooms, restaurants, spas, meeting rooms, add-ons) —
paginated and filterable.

Returns PERMISSION_DENIED when the property exists but is not in your sales channel, and PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_NOT_FOUND
when the property identifier is unknown, so you can tell the two apart the same way the REST twin's
403/404 split lets you. Billed 1 unit per property whose media is returned.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

post.description:
List media across multiple properties

Batch gallery retrieval across up to 20 properties in one call — built for a nightly or hourly sync
job rather than a page render. A bad property identifier never fails the whole batch: each entry
carries its own status (`PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_OK`, `PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_NOT_IN_CHANNEL`, `PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`) instead.

Billed 1 unit per property whose media is returned — that is, per entry with status `PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_OK`. A
`PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_NOT_IN_CHANNEL` or `PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_NOT_FOUND` entry costs nothing.

200.description: The RPC completed with gRPC status OK.

userSession.description: Traveller context: dates, occupancy, language and currency. Required.

searchFilters.description: Optional narrowing of the result set.

size.description:
Results per page. Defaults to 20, which is also the maximum. A larger value is rejected with
INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than clamped, so a caller never pages through a result set believing it is
larger than it is. Every property returned is billed, so the cap bounds cost as well as fan-out.

wink.partner.v1.SearchByGeoRequest.description:
Request for SearchByGeo.

At most one of `location, bounds` is set (protobuf `oneof area`).

itinerary.description: Stay dates and occupancy. Required — searches without an itinerary cannot be priced.

language.description:
ISO 639-1 language, e.g. "en". Affects the little text this surface returns; for descriptions and other
prose, pass the language to the Content service instead. Defaults to "en".

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency for all returned prices, e.g. "THB". Exactly three characters. Defaults to the
property's own currency.

promotionalCodes.description: Promotional codes to apply. Codes your account is not entitled to are ignored, not rejected.

wink.partner.v1.UserSession.description:
Who is travelling, when, and in what currency and language.

This drives pricing, not just presentation: `currency` selects the currency every Money on the response is
converted into, and `itinerary` determines both availability and how the call is billed.

startDate.description:
Check-in date, ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DD". Required. Must be today or later -- a past date is rejected
with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

nights.description: Number of nights. Billing caps this at 90; a longer stay is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

rooms.description:
The rooms being searched for. Supply at least one. Multiple entries search for several rooms at
once — two adults in one room and a family of four in another is two entries, not two searches.

adults.description: Adults in this room. Defaults to 1.

children.description:
Children in this room, by age. Ages are REQUIRED, not optional detail: properties price children in
age bands, and an unpriceable age produces a rate the guest cannot actually book.

quantity.description: How many identical rooms of this configuration. Defaults to 1.

age.description:
Age at check-in, in years. Zero is valid — infants are priced differently from older children, not
ignored.

quantity.description: How many children of this age. Defaults to 1.

wink.partner.v1.ChildOccupancy.description: A number of children of the same age.

type.description: Always "Point". Present so the value round-trips as valid GeoJSON.

wink.partner.v1.GeoPoint.description:
A geographic point, GeoJSON-style.

Mirrors the GeoJSON `Point` the REST API emits: `type` is always `"Point"` and `coordinates` is
`[longitude, latitude]` — in that order, which is GeoJSON's and is the REVERSE of the `lat,lng` ordering
most mapping UIs use. Getting this backwards places properties in the wrong hemisphere, so it is worth
asserting in your client tests.

wink.partner.v1.MapBounds.description: A rectangular map viewport, for SearchByGeo.

radiusInMeters.description: Radius around `location`, in metres. Only meaningful for SearchByGeo with a point.

lifestyle.description: Restrict to properties oriented toward this lifestyle.

directOnly.description: Only properties bookable direct, excluding intermediated inventory.

displayCurrency.description:
ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in — the one you asked for in
`user_session.currency`, or the property's own when you asked for none. Stated once here rather than
repeated on every amount, which is why the amounts themselves are bare integers.

currencyExponent.description:
How many decimal places `display_currency` has: 2 for THB and USD, 0 for JPY, KRW and VND.

Amounts are integers in MINOR UNITS, so the real value is `amount / 10^currency_exponent`. This is
published rather than assumed because a fixed divide-by-100 is wrong for a real slice of Wink's
inventory — a JPY stay priced at 15000 is ¥15,000, not ¥150.

displayLanguage.description:
ISO 639-1 language the names and other text in this response are in — the one you asked for in
`user_session.language`, or English when it was unavailable.

totalElements.description: Total matching properties across all pages.

numberOfElements.description: Properties on this page. Differs from `size` on the last page.

first.description: True if this is the first page.

last.description: True if this is the last page.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyPage.description:
One page of priced properties.

Wire mirror of the REST PageResponse envelope: `number` is zero-based and `total_elements` counts across
all pages, not this one.

propertyId.description: Stable property identifier. Your key for everything, including Content lookups.

urlName.description: Url-safe slug, stable and safe to build links from.

uniqueId.description: The property's globally unique short code.

name.description:
Property name in the requested language. Enough to label a result row; full localized content comes
from the Content service.

location.description: Where the property is, for map pins and distance sorting.

starRating.description: Official star rating, 1-5. Zero when unrated.

heroImage.description: A single representative image for the result row. The complete gallery is in Content.

lastUpdate.description:
When this property's record last changed, ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss" in UTC.

Use it as the cache key for your Content responses: store it alongside what you fetched, compare on
each search, and re-fetch only when it has moved. It advances when the property or any inventory item
beneath it is added, removed or edited.

A caveat worth knowing before you rely on it for correctness: it tracks the property AGGREGATE, so an
edit confined to a child entity's prose may not always advance it. Treat a stale read as possible and
re-sync periodically regardless.

prices.description:
Priced offers, SORTED CHEAPEST FIRST by `total`. `prices[0]` is the property's best available
price.

commission.description:
Commission rate your account earns on this property, as a fraction — 0.15 for 15%. A property-channel
term rather than a per-rate one: it describes your commercial relationship with the property, so it
holds for every offer below.

A double rather than a float because this multiplies money. 0.15 has no exact binary representation,
and the wider type keeps the error far enough below a minor unit that `total * commission` does not
drift into a visible discrepancy on large bookings.

direct.description: True if this is direct inventory, with no intermediary between you and the property.

available.description:
True if AT LEAST ONE room type at this property is bookable for the itinerary. Per-room-type
availability is `RoomPrice.available`; this is the "is anything here bookable at all" flag. When false,
`prices` still carries the unavailable offers rather than being empty, so you can show why.

wink.partner.v1.PropertySearchResult.description:
One property and its live prices.

Carries only what a result list needs to render, plus the prices. For anything else about the property —
descriptions, full gallery, address, amenities, room detail, policies — call the Content service with
`property_id` and cache the answer against `last_update`.

mediaId.description: Stable identifier for this asset. Use this as your cache key.

entityId.description:
Identifier of the inventory item this asset belongs to (the property, a guest room, and so on).
Named `entity_id` rather than `identifier` to match the `*_id` convention the rest of this surface
uses, and because "identifier" said nothing about WHOSE identifier it is.

source.description: Where the asset came from, e.g. the property's own upload or a syndicated source.

sort.description: Display order within its gallery, ascending.

angle.description: Camera angle or shot description, when the property supplied one.

lifestyleType.description: The lifestyle this asset is meant to illustrate, when tagged.

urls.description:
Ready-to-use delivery URLs, one per variant. Which variants are populated depends on whether the
asset is an image, a Cloudinary video or an externally-hosted one — see MediaUrlSet.

wink.partner.v1.Multimedia.description:
One published image or video.

Key anything you cache on `media_id`. It is stable for the life of the asset; URLs are not — they
carry transformation and delivery parameters that change without notice.

wink.partner.v1.Description.description:
A short piece of localized text.

The API returns descriptions already filtered to the language on your request, so you will normally see
exactly one entry per collection. `language` is still present so you can tell which language you got when
the requested one was unavailable and the property's default was substituted.

original.description: MEDIA_TYPE_IMAGE only: unscaled, best-quality delivery URL.

large.description: MEDIA_TYPE_IMAGE only: large variant, max width 1920px.

medium.description: MEDIA_TYPE_IMAGE only: medium variant, max width 1024px.

thumbnail.description:
MEDIA_TYPE_IMAGE or MEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO (Cloudinary): thumbnail variant, max width 320px. For video this is a jpg frame
extracted from the video.

stream.description: MEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO (Cloudinary) only: mp4 streaming delivery URL, unscaled.

preview.description: MEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO (Cloudinary) only: mp4 preview variant, max width 1280px.

poster.description: MEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO (Cloudinary) only: poster frame, a jpg still extracted from the video at medium width.

externalUrl.description:
MEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO (YouTube) only: pass-through to the YouTube watch URL. Wink generates no variants for
externally-hosted media.

wink.partner.v1.MediaUrlSet.description:
Ready-to-use delivery URLs for one asset, one field per variant.

Which fields are populated depends on the asset. Images carry `original`, `large`, `medium` and
`thumbnail`; Cloudinary videos carry `stream`, `preview`, `poster` and `thumbnail`; externally-hosted
video (YouTube) carries only `external_url`, because Wink generates no variants for media it does not
host. Always check the variant you want is present rather than assuming a fixed set.

THESE URLS MAY ROTATE. Wink's media-reorganization migration rewrites the underlying storage id of
every asset it touches, which changes every URL here. `Multimedia.media_id` does NOT change. Key your
storage on `media_id` and re-sync when `PropertySearchResult.content_version` moves; treating a URL as a
permanent identifier will break.

url.description: Ready-to-use delivery URL for this variant.

maxWidth.description:
Maximum pixel width this variant is scaled to. Unset for variants with no resize (image
"original", video "stream") — explicit presence so "not resized" is distinguishable from a
literal 0px width.

format.description: Delivery format label for this variant.

wink.partner.v1.MediaUrlVariant.description: One delivery URL and what it is scaled to.

roomRateId.description:
Room rate identifier. Join to Content for the room type, rate plan (embedded on the master rate),
descriptions, images and amenities behind this offer.

name.description:
The ROOM TYPE's name, localized — "Deluxe King Room" and the like. Enough to label the offer in a
result list; the full description, images and amenities are in Content.

In `user_session.language` when the property has translated it, otherwise English, otherwise whatever
the property supplied. A row labelled in the wrong language is still more use than a blank one.

available.description:
True if THIS offer, at the requested occupancy, is bookable for the itinerary. Narrower than
`PropertySearchResult.available`, which is true when ANY offer at the property is. An unavailable offer is
still returned rather than dropped, so you can show the traveller why it cannot be booked.

sort.description: Ordering hint within the property's offers, ascending.

adults.description: Adults the rate is priced for, after the property's occupancy policy is applied.

children.description: Children the rate is priced for, after the property's occupancy policy is applied.

roomTotalBeforeDiscount.description:
The property's price for the ROOM over the whole stay BEFORE promotions, premiums and your channel
discount — step 1 above. Show it struck through next to `room_total` to display the saving.

Equal to `room_total` when no adjustment applies. It can also be LOWER than `room_total` when a premium
is in force, since premiums travel the same path as discounts — so only render a strikethrough when
this is actually the greater of the two.

roomTotal.description:
Cost of the ROOM over the whole stay, after promotions, premiums and your channel discount — step 2
above. Excludes the rate plan's fixed extra charges.

Named `room_total`, not `source_total`, on purpose: everywhere else in this platform "source" means the
PROPERTY'S OWN CURRENCY, and this figure is in the caller's. Reusing the word here would have had the
next mapper author reach for the domain's `getSourceTotal()` and quote the wrong currency.

extraChargesTotal.description:
Fixed charges attached to the rate plan — a one-time cleaning fee and the like — over the whole stay.
Reported separately so a traveller can see them as their own line rather than as an unexplained
difference. Never discounted. Zero when the rate plan has none.

total.description:
What the guest pays: `room_total` + `extra_charges_total`. This is the number to show.

Only meaningful when `available` is true. An unavailable offer reports 0 across all four amounts, which
means "not priced" rather than "free" — show the offer with its reason, never with a price of zero.

meals.description:
Meals included in the rate. These change which offer a traveller picks, so they are here rather than
behind an identifier.

refundable.description: True if the stay can be cancelled without charge before the policy's deadline.

refundableUntilDays.description:
How many days from TODAY the traveller has left to cancel free of charge, and -1 when the rate is not
refundable at all. Zero means the free-cancellation window closes today.

Derived as (days until check-in) − (the policy's days-before-arrival deadline), floored at 0 — the same
calculation `RoomTypeBestPriceForDateRange` publishes. It is relative to the moment of the response and
will drift as the stay approaches, so treat it as display data, not something to cache.

cancellationPolicyId.description: Cancellation policy identifier. Join to Content for the full terms and wording.

perkIds.description:
Identifiers of the perks bundled with this rate. Join to Content for their names and descriptions.
There is deliberately no monetary "perk value" on this surface.

wink.partner.v1.RoomRate.description:
One priced, bookable offer for the itinerary.

Everything here either is a price or changes which offer a traveller would choose. The prose behind the
identifiers — rate plan names, perk descriptions, cancellation policy wording — lives in Content, reached
via `room_rate_id`.

HOW THE PRICE IS BUILT, and what each field means:

  1. The property gives Wink a base price for the room over these dates. That is
     `room_total_before_discount` — the "was" price.
  2. Promotions, premiums and your channel discount are applied to it. The result is `room_total` —
     the cost of the ROOM ITSELF, all adjustments applied. This is the "now" price.
  3. Fixed charges attached to the rate plan are added — a one-time cleaning fee and the like. They are
     a distinct cost, so they are reported separately as `extra_charges_total` rather than folded in,
     and a traveller can see what they are paying for.

  room_total + extra_charges_total = total

MONEY CONVENTION. Every monetary field is `<component>_total`, covers the WHOLE stay, and is an INTEGER
IN MINOR UNITS of `PropertyPage.display_currency` — divide by 10^`PropertyPage.currency_exponent` to get
the real value. The currency and its exponent are stated once per page instead of on every amount, so the
amounts are directly comparable and directly addable with exact integer arithmetic and no rounding.
`total` is the only one with no component prefix, because it is the sum of them all and the number to
show as the price.

Discounts apply to the ROOM only, never to extra charges — a cleaning fee is not discounted. So the
saving a traveller sees is exactly `room_total_before_discount - room_total`.

geoNameId.description: GeoNames id of the city, as returned by the Lookup service. Required.

searchFilters.description: Optional narrowing of the result set.

size.description:
Results per page. Defaults to 20, which is also the maximum. A larger value is rejected with
INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than clamped, so a caller never pages through a result set believing it is
larger than it is. Every property returned is billed, so the cap bounds cost as well as fan-out.

repeated on every amount, which is why the amounts themselves are bare integers.

Amounts are integers in MINOR UNITS, so the real value is `amount / 10^currency_exponent`. This is
published rather than assumed because a fixed divide-by-100 is wrong for a real slice of Wink's
inventory — a JPY stay priced at 15000 is ¥15,000, not ¥150.

displayLanguage.description:
ISO 639-1 language the names and other text in this response are in — the one you asked for in
`user_session.language`, or English when it was unavailable.

cityUrlNameOrCountryCode.description: City url name or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code scoping the agency's properties. Required.

Results per page. Defaults to 20, which is also the maximum. A larger value is rejected with
INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than clamped, so a caller never pages through a result set believing it is
larger than it is. Every property returned is billed, so the cap bounds cost as well as fan-out.

displayCurrency.description:
ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in — the one you asked for in
`user_session.currency`, or the property's own when you asked for none. Stated once here rather than
repeated on every amount, which is why the amounts themselves are bare integers.

How many decimal places `display_currency` has: 2 for THB and USD, 0 for JPY, KRW and VND.

Amounts are integers in MINOR UNITS, so the real value is `amount / 10^currency_exponent`. This is
published rather than assumed because a fixed divide-by-100 is wrong for a real slice of Wink's
inventory — a JPY stay priced at 15000 is ¥15,000, not ¥150.

displayLanguage.description:
ISO 639-1 language the names and other text in this response are in — the one you asked for in
`user_session.language`, or English when it was unavailable.

urlName.description: Url name of the city, as returned by the Lookup service. Required.

searchFilters.description: Optional narrowing of the result set.

size.description:
Results per page. Defaults to 20, which is also the maximum. A larger value is rejected with
INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than clamped, so a caller never pages through a result set believing it is
larger than it is. Every property returned is billed, so the cap bounds cost as well as fan-out.

displayCurrency.description:
ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in — the one you asked for in
`user_session.currency`, or the property's own when you asked for none. Stated once here rather than
repeated on every amount, which is why the amounts themselves are bare integers.

currencyExponent.description:
How many decimal places `display_currency` has: 2 for THB and USD, 0 for JPY, KRW and VND.

Amounts are integers in MINOR UNITS, so the real value is `amount / 10^currency_exponent`. This is
published rather than assumed because a fixed divide-by-100 is wrong for a real slice of Wink's
inventory — a JPY stay priced at 15000 is ¥15,000, not ¥150.

term.description:
What the user has typed so far. Fewer than 3 characters (after trimming) returns an empty
list rather than an error.

wink.partner.v1.SearchRequest.description:
Your Wink account identifier. Every call is scoped to one account, and your token must hold
INVENTORY:READ on it.

destinations.description: Matching destinations, most relevant first. At most 50.

id.description: Wink's identifier for this destination entry.

type.description: What kind of place this is. Determines what `type_identifier` refers to.

typeIdentifier.description:
Identifier of the underlying resource — a property ID for DESTINATION_TYPE_PROPERTY, a geoname ID for DESTINATION_TYPE_CITY and
DESTINATION_TYPE_COUNTRY. This is the id you pass to the other Wink endpoints that take a property or place.

name.description: Display name, in the language given by `language_code`.

urlName.description: URL slug. Pass this back to the lookup-by-slug call to resolve this destination later.

ownerName.description: Display name of the supplier that created this entry, where one applies.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-1 code for the language `name` is written in.

longitude.description:
Longitude and latitude in decimal degrees. Both are omitted together when the location is
unknown — which is why they are optional rather than defaulting to 0/0, a real place in the
Gulf of Guinea.

wink.partner.v1.Destination.description: A place you can search for and sell through Wink.

urlName.description: URL slug of the destination, e.g. `bangkok-thailand`. Required.

type.description:
Type of the destination you are resolving. Required — a slug is only unique within a type,
so leaving this unset is rejected rather than guessed.

wink.partner.v1.GetRequest.description:
Your Wink account identifier. Every call is scoped to one account, and your token must hold
INVENTORY:READ on it.

userSession.description: Traveller context: dates, occupancy, language and currency. Required.

propertyId.description: Stable property identifier, as returned by Search and Lookup.

urlName.description: Url-safe slug, as returned by Search.

wink.partner.v1.GetPropertyInventoryRequ.description:
Request for GetPropertyInventory.

At most one of `propertyId, urlName` is set (protobuf `oneof property`).

displayCurrency.description: ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in.

currencyExponent.description: How many decimal places `display_currency` has — amounts are `amount / 10^currency_exponent`.

displayLanguage.description: ISO 639-1 language the names in this response are in.

propertyId.description: Stable property identifier. Your key for everything, including Content lookups.

urlName.description: Url-safe slug, stable and safe to build links from.

uniqueId.description: The property's globally unique short code.

lastUpdate.description:
When this property's record last changed, ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss" in UTC. Use it as the cache key
for your Content responses — the same value Search returns.

available.description:
True if AT LEAST ONE offer is bookable for the requested stay. When false, `prices` still carries the
unavailable offers rather than being empty, so you can show why.

commission.description:
Commission rate your account earns on this property, as a fraction — 0.15 for 15%. A property-channel
term, so it holds for every offer below.

prices.description:
EVERY priced offer for the requested stay, SORTED CHEAPEST FIRST by `total`.

This is where Inventory differs from Search: Search returns the best offer per room type, this returns
every rate and occupancy combination the property has for these dates. `prices[0]` is the best available
price, the same figure Search would have shown for this property.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyInventory.description:
One property and every priced offer available for the requested stay.

For anything else about the property — name, descriptions, gallery, address, amenities, policies, and its
restaurants, spas, meeting rooms and activities — call the Content service with `property_id` and cache the
answer against `last_update`.

entries.description:
The properties to price, each with its own dates and occupancy. At least one, at most 20.

Every entry must ask for the SAME `user_session.currency` and `user_session.language`, because the
response declares one display currency for all of them. A batch that mixes currencies is rejected with
INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than answered in a currency half the entries did not ask for.

properties.description:
One entry per request entry, in the order requested — match results back to your request by position.

The batch is ATOMIC. If any property cannot be resolved the whole call fails rather than returning a
short or reordered list, because a partial response that still looked well-formed would have you
attribute one property's prices to another. Nothing is billed for a failed batch.

displayCurrency.description: ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in.

currencyExponent.description: How many decimal places `display_currency` has — amounts are `amount / 10^currency_exponent`.

displayLanguage.description: ISO 639-1 language the names in this response are in.

startDate.description: First check-in date to price, ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DD". Required.

periodInDays.description:
How many days forward to price from `start_date`. Between 2 and 30. Required.

This is also the billed unit count: a 30-day calendar costs 30 hotel-day units.

adults.description: Adults per room, between 1 and 10. Omit it to take the default of 2.

language.description:
ISO 639-1 language for the room names, e.g. "en". Required: room names are translated against it,
and with no language supplied every name falls back to its untranslated form.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency for the returned prices. Exactly three characters.

ratePlanNameMatches.description:
Optional regular expression restricting the calendar to rate plans whose name matches — useful for
pricing only your negotiated plans. Left unset, every rate plan is considered.

At most 256 characters. Matching additionally runs under a fixed input budget, so a pathological pattern
is abandoned rather than allowed to burn server time.

displayCurrency.description: ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in.

currencyExponent.description: How many decimal places `display_currency` has — amounts are `amount / 10^currency_exponent`.

displayLanguage.description: ISO 639-1 language the names in this response are in.

name.description: The property's name, in the requested language.

adults.description:
Adults every rate in this calendar is priced for — the occupancy you asked for, so it is the same for
every entry and is stated once here rather than repeated on each.

internetIncluded.description: True if internet is included across the priced rates.

parkingIncluded.description: True if parking is included across the priced rates.

entries.description: One entry per check-in/check-out combination in the range.

wink.partner.v1.RatePeriod.description: Best available rate for each check-in date across the requested range.

roomTypeId.description: Identifier of the room type this rate is for. Join to Content for its description, images and amenities.

name.description: The room type's name, in the requested language.

available.description: True if this combination is bookable.

refundable.description: True if it can be cancelled without charge before the policy's deadline.

refundableUntilDays.description:
Days from TODAY until free cancellation closes; -1 when not refundable, 0 when it closes today. Same
calculation as `RoomRate.refundable_until_days`.

total.description:
What the guest pays for this combination, in minor units of `display_currency`.

Only meaningful when `available` is true. An unavailable combination reports 0, which means "no price"
rather than "free" — do not render it as a price.

wink.partner.v1.RatePeriodEntry.description: The best available rate for one check-in/check-out combination.

propertyId.description: The property to retrieve media for. Required.

mediaTypes.description: Restrict results to these media types. Leave empty for both images and videos.

inventoryTypes.description:
Restrict results to these galleries. Leave empty for every gallery (property plus all entitled
inventory types).

inventoryIdentifier.description:
Restrict results to a single inventory item's gallery, e.g. one room type. Combine with
inventory_types to disambiguate the type. Ignored when inventory_types selects PROPERTY only.

categories.description: Restrict results to these OTA PIC photo-category codes. Leave empty for every category.

language.description: Language to prune captions to. Falls back to English when omitted.

size.description: Page size, max 200. Defaults to 50 when unset (0).

wink.partner.v1.GetPropertyMediaRequest.description:
Your Wink account identifier. Every call is scoped to one account, and your token must hold
INVENTORY:READ on it.

propertyId.description: Property identifier, echoed from the request.

media.description: Paginated, filtered gallery for this property.

totalElements.description: Total number of assets across all pages.

totalPages.description: Total number of pages for the current page size.

numberOfElements.description: Number of assets actually on this page.

first.description: Whether this is the first page.

last.description: Whether this is the last page.

wink.partner.v1.MediaPage.description:
A page of media assets plus flat page metadata — the wire mirror of the REST envelope every
paginated Wink endpoint returns.

mediaIdentifier.description:
Stable media identifier — key your integration on this, not on any URL. It survives the
platform's media reorganization, which rewrites the underlying storage path (and therefore
every delivery URL) without changing this identifier.

inventoryType.description: Which gallery this asset belongs to.

inventoryIdentifier.description:
Identifier of the owning inventory item (room type, restaurant, spa, meeting room, add-on).
Unset when inventory_type is PROPERTY.

inventoryName.description: Display name of the owning inventory item, or the property name when inventory_type is PROPERTY.

mediaType.description: Whether this asset is an image or video.

source.description: Hosting platform this asset is served from.

sort.description: Display order within the owning gallery. Lower sorts first.

width.description: Media width in pixels. 0 when unavailable (e.g. YouTube).

height.description: Media height in pixels. 0 when unavailable (e.g. YouTube).

caption.description:
Caption/alt text pruned to the requested language, falling back to English. Unset when no
description is set.

lifestyleType.description:
Lifestyle association for this asset, if any. LIFESTYLE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED means none is set —
this field is genuinely optional, unlike a request-side type selector.

urls.description: Fixed set of ready-to-use delivery-URL variants for this asset.

wink.partner.v1.MediaAsset.description:
One published media asset (image or video) belonging to a property or one of its bookable inventory
items.

url.description: URL to the contributor's profile, if any.

name.description: Name of the contributor. Required whenever an attribution entry is present.

wink.partner.v1.MediaAttribution.description: Photographer/source attribution for one media asset.

propertyIds.description: Properties to retrieve media for, 1 to 20 entries. Required.

mediaTypes.description:
Restrict results to these media types, applied to every property in the batch. Leave empty for
both images and videos.

inventoryTypes.description:
Restrict results to these galleries, applied to every property in the batch. Leave empty for
every gallery.

inventoryIdentifier.description: Restrict results to a single inventory item's gallery, applied to every property in the batch.

categories.description: Restrict results to these OTA PIC photo-category codes, applied to every property in the batch.

language.description: Language to prune captions to, applied to every property in the batch. Falls back to English.

perPropertyLimit.description: Maximum assets returned per property, max 200. Defaults to 50 when unset (0).

wink.partner.v1.ListMediaRequest.description:
Your Wink account identifier. Every call is scoped to one account, and your token must hold
INVENTORY:READ on it.

properties.description:
One entry per property identifier in the request, same order. Always as many entries as you
requested — a batch never fails as a whole for one bad property identifier.

propertyId.description: Property identifier, echoed from the request.

propertyName.description: Property name. Unset unless status is PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_OK.

status.description: Whether this property's media was retrieved, and if not, why.

totalAssets.description:
Total published assets matching the filter, before per_property_limit truncation. 0 unless status
is PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_OK.

assets.description:
Media assets for this property, truncated to the request's per_property_limit. Empty unless status is
PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_OK.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyMediaEntry.description: One property's outcome within a batch ListMedia response.

wink.partner.v1.LifestyleType.description:
The traveller lifestyle a property, room or media asset is oriented toward.

Values are additive: a property may carry several. Treat an unrecognized value as "some lifestyle this
client does not know about yet" rather than an error — proto3 enums are open, and new lifestyles are
added without a version bump.

- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_HEALTH_FITNESS`: Health and fitness focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_RELAX`: Relaxation focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_ADULT_ONLY`: Adults only.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_ADVENTURE`: Adventure travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_BUSINESS`: Business travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_LGBT`: LGBT focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SINGLE_PARENT`: Single parent travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SOLO_FEMALE`: Solo female travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_BEAUTY`: Beauty and wellness.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_FOODIE`: Food and dining focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_FAMILY`: Family travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_ROMANCE`: Romantic travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_COUPLE`: Couples travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SOLO`: Solo travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_BACKPACKER`: Backpacking.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SHOPPING`: Shopping focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SPORTS`: Sports focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_MOUNTAIN`: Mountain destinations.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_BEACH`: Beach destinations.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_CITY`: City destinations.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_COUNTRY`: Countryside destinations.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_CULTURE`: Culture and heritage.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_ECO`: Eco and sustainable travel.

wink.partner.v1.MultimediaKind.description:
Whether a Media entry is a still image or a video.

- `MULTIMEDIA_KIND_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set.
- `MULTIMEDIA_KIND_IMAGE`: A still image.
- `MULTIMEDIA_KIND_VIDEO`: A video.

wink.partner.v1.ScoreSort.description:
How ranked results are ordered.

Four orderings, and they are the only four the platform actually has. Wink previously scored properties
on separate member, popularity, experience, perk, loyalty and add-on dimensions; those collapsed into a
single demand score in 2026-07 and their backing fields no longer exist. The REST enum keeps them as
deprecated aliases so persisted documents keep loading — every one silently resolves to RECOMMENDED —
but this contract is new, so it publishes only what it can honour. A sort you can select and that does
nothing is worse than one you cannot select.

- `SCORE_SORT_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set; the server picks RECOMMENDED.
- `SCORE_SORT_RECOMMENDED`: Wink's demand score — bookings and reviews blended, 0-100. The default.
- `SCORE_SORT_PRICE_LOW_TO_HIGH`: Cheapest first.
- `SCORE_SORT_PRICE_HIGH_TO_LOW`: Most expensive first.
- `SCORE_SORT_ECO`: Sustainability, highest first — backed by the green-index rating, which is maintained separately from the demand score.

wink.partner.v1.DestinationType.description:
What kind of place a destination is.

- `DESTINATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Never sent by the server, and rejected on a request: pick a real type.

wink.partner.v1.MediaType.description:
Classifies the format of a media asset.

- `MEDIA_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Never sent by the server on a real asset.

wink.partner.v1.MediaInventoryScope.description:
Which gallery a media asset belongs to: the property itself, or a bookable inventory type.

Values are prefixed MEDIA_ (unlike DestinationType's bare DESTINATION_TYPE_CITY/DESTINATION_TYPE_PROPERTY/etc.) because proto3 enum
values are siblings within the whole `wink.partner.v1` package, not scoped to their enum type —
DestinationType in partner_destination_lookup.proto already claims DESTINATION_TYPE_RESTAURANT, DESTINATION_TYPE_SPA and
DESTINATION_TYPE_MEETING_ROOM, and protoc rejects the redefinition outright.

- `MEDIA_INVENTORY_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED`: On a response asset this is never sent; on a request filter it is simply never included in the repeated field (an empty repeated field already means "no restriction").

wink.partner.v1.MediaSource.description:
Identifies the hosting platform a media asset is served from.

- `MEDIA_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED`: Never sent by the server on a real asset.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyMediaStatus.description:
Per-property outcome of a batch ListMedia entry.

- `PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED`: Never sent by the server for a resolvable entry; present only so the zero value is not a real status.
- `PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_OK`: The property is entitled to the requesting account; property_name/assets are populated.
- `PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_NOT_IN_CHANNEL`: The property exists but is not in the requesting account's sales channel. property_name/assets are empty.
- `PROPERTY_MEDIA_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`: No property with this identifier exists. property_name/assets are empty.

oauth2ClientCredentials.description:
Every endpoint is protected with OAuth2 **client credentials**. Create an
**Application** in your account to obtain a `clientId` and `clientSecret`, then
exchange them for a short-lived bearer token.

### 1. Request an access token
`POST` to the **Token URL** below with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
and a body of `grant_type=client_credentials` (optionally `scope=<space-separated scopes>`).
Send your credentials as HTTP Basic auth:
`Authorization: Basic base64(clientId + ":" + clientSecret)`.

### 2. Call the API
Pass the returned token on every request: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

Tokens carry only the scopes granted to your Application — request the least privilege
you need. There is no interactive authorize step and no refresh token for this flow;
request a new token when the current one expires.
oauth2ClientCredentials.name: Client Credentials

scopes.inventory.write: Create and update your inventory & rates.
